clue.text: Insane, having a fossil-fuel vehicle in this island

parts.note: insane means mad
gas is a fossil fuel (natural gas, or petrol in American usage)
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone crazy is driving a petrol-guzzling car around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'this island' points back at the whole clue: the island built from MAD + A GAS CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is a large island nation off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Mike has to request lockdown accessory

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Mike has been told to ask for something to wear during lockdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Face coverings were the item everyone carried during the pandemic lockdowns, hence an accessory of that period.

clue.text: 'Expressionless, unexciting' — review unfavourably

parts.note: a dead party or town is unexciting
critics pan a show they dislike

explanation.surface: A critic's damning verdict: blank and dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no emotion, which is the sense of expressionless.

clue.text: A little bee getting hog agitated? No — it's an enormous insect

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of these words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Is that a little bee annoying a pig? No, it's a gigantic bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges A LITTLE BEE plus HOG; 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goliath beetle of Africa is among the heaviest insects in the world, named after the biblical giant.

clue.text: Using drugs looking for partner in the Home Counties?

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in South East England, abbreviated SE
someone dating is seeking a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A question about romance among the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedating means calming a patient by giving them drugs, so it describes someone administering medication.

clue.text: Spot some jelly in Nigella's pictures

indicators.note: to spot is to find, here finding the answer tucked inside the words Nigella's pictures

explanation.surface: Look for a wobbly dish in a TV cook's photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson is a British TV cook, which makes the jelly feel natural. The answer runs across NigellASPICtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Order leader of yeomen to follow command

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of yeomen

explanation.surface: An instruction for the head of a band of yeomen to do as told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb meaning command, but it is the OBE, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to comply with an instruction, so it is to follow a command.

clue.text: Make notes on this and get degrees before too long

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees
soon means before too long

explanation.surface: Advice to a student: take notes and graduate quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests studying; here it means playing music.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoon is a woodwind instrument, something you produce musical notes on.

clue.text: Past agreement with heartless Terence needs attention

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the name, its heart

parts.note: Terry is the usual short form of the name Terence
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A deal made long ago with a callous man named Terence must be looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence must first become Terry; 'heartless' removes its central R to leave TERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means times gone by, the past, as a noun.

clue.text: Obstruct a place in the market

definitions.meaning: a trader's stand in a market

explanation.definitionFit: Stall is both a verb for blocking or holding up and a noun for a market trader's pitch.

clue.text: Stands in seeds I put out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener describes planting: seeds that have been put out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deputises substitutes for another person, stands in for them.

clue.text: Message going to eastern European — with this?

definitions.text: Message going to eastern European — with this?

parts.note: to telegraph is to send a message by wire
a Pole comes from Poland in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A wire being sent to someone in Poland, and asking how.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: telegraph messages were carried on wires strung between these.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegraph poles carried the overhead wires along which telegrams travelled.

clue.text: Despite its name, it's normally neither useful nor amusing!

definitions.text: Despite its name, it's normally neither useful nor amusing!

parts.words: Despite its name, it's normally neither useful nor amusing!
parts.note: the name of this prank contains a word for useful and a word for something funny, yet the thing itself is often neither

explanation.definitionFit: A practical joke is a prank played on someone, rarely practical and often not funny to the victim.

clue.text: Mark redeployed as organisation's first prophet

indicators.note: redeployed means rearranged into new positions, so these letters are reordered
first takes the opening letter of organisation's

explanation.surface: A man named Mark, moved to a new post, becomes the organisation's leading prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeployed' rearranges AS, O (the first letter of 'organisation's') and PROPHET. 'Mark' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark showing possession or omission.

clue.text: Liking to write church music?

parts.note: to pen is to write
chant is sung music in church services

explanation.surface: Fondness for composing liturgical song.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or fondness for something.

clue.text: Long time with northern Conservative getting unknown sales interests

parts.note: an age is a long time
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A northern Tory, after many years, takes on business interests in sales.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a business representing a company's commercial interests, such as selling its products.

clue.text: Stars displeased — son and daughter missing — becoming agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the remaining letters are shuffled
missing means these letters are absent from the word displeased

explanation.surface: Celebrities are unhappy and upset when their children go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes S and D out of DISPLEASED to leave IPLEASED; 'becoming agitated' rearranges it. 'Stars' looks like celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pleiades are a cluster of stars in the constellation Taurus, the Seven Sisters.

clue.text: Galloping horse with just a light rein, we hear?

indicators.note: a galloping horse is in wild motion, so its letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A rider lets a horse gallop with only slight control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galloping' rearranges HORSE and W. The definition is a sound pun: 'light rein' sounds like light rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a brief spell of light rain, and rain sounds the same as rein.

clue.text: Utensils provided for cricketers

definitions.meaning: tools for opening tins and bottles
the two batsmen who begin a cricket innings

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen start the side's innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Opener names both a kitchen gadget for tins and bottles and a batsman who starts the innings.

clue.text: Balham renovated by painter in palace

indicators.note: renovated means done up and rebuilt, so the letters of Balham are reworked

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: An artist restores a home in Balham, a district of south London, to palatial grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Stopping near, doctor primarily should achieve such a manner

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so a letter is put into the middle of the word for near

parts.note: beside means near

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor, close at hand, ought chiefly to show a good way with patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' puts D, the first letter of 'doctor', inside BESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's bedside manner is the way they treat and talk to patients.

clue.text: Renewed and rebuilt tables in back of major English independent workshop

indicators.note: in puts the rebuilt word inside the other letters
the back of a word is its last letter, here of major

parts.note: a shed is often used as a workshop

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together in a new form, so the letters of tables are rearranged

explanation.surface: Furniture remade in the back of a big independent English workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tables' looks like furniture being made, but 'rebuilt' only shuffles its letters; 'in' then sets them inside the rest, with 'back of' picking the final letter of 'major'.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-established means restored or set up again, as something renewed is.

clue.text: Inclination to get book for pound, all else being equal

indicators.note: book for pound means the letter for book takes the place of the letter for pound

parts.note: with everything equal, things are level
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bookie's sense of tilt when weighing a book against a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the first L of LEVEL for B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevel is a sloping edge or surface, an angle of inclination.

clue.text: Marries in midweek?

definitions.meaning: The abbreviation for Wednesdays, the middle of the week

explanation.definitionFit: Weds is a verb for marrying and also the short form of Wednesdays, days in the middle of the week.

clue.text: Like chutney perhaps, put on the table in advance?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before, in advance
served means put food on the table

explanation.surface: Was the relish brought out early?
explanation.definitionFit: Chutney is a preserve: fruit or vegetables kept in vinegar and sugar.

clue.text: Zero movement in such a window

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
give is the slight movement or flexibility in something

explanation.surface: A window that does not budge at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogive is a pointed Gothic arch, so an ogive window is one with that pointed head.

clue.text: Queen leaves festival in this direction

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so these letters go out of the word for the festival

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch departs a celebration heading one way.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass points, a direction of travel.

clue.text: Does their work make them go up the wall?

definitions.text: Does their work make them go up the wall?

parts.words: Does their work make them go up the wall?
parts.note: going up the wall means getting exasperated, but these tradesmen literally spread their material up walls

explanation.definitionFit: Plasterers are tradespeople who apply plaster to walls and ceilings.
